change_family: CF-01 Actor identity and mandate extension
current_v2_component: Actor entity (Draft V2 section 4 Identity Rules) has no continuity/mandate/non-identity fields
proposed_v2_1_component: Add OPTIONAL fields to the Actor entity: mandate_status, mandate_scope, identity_continuity_status, explicit_non_identity_with (list of actor_ids the researcher has deliberately determined NOT to be the same actor, with rationale)
problem_solved: Removes the need for each case artifact to reinvent ad hoc, non-interoperable extension fields (already happening identically across V2/V3/V4); enables a future generalized validator to check actor-identity discipline consistently
schema_change: Yes -- 4 new optional fields on Actor
controlled_vocabulary_change: No new controlled-vocabulary enum values for relation_type or entity classes; mandate_status/continuity_status become semi-structured free-text-with-guidance fields, not closed enumerations, to avoid overfitting to only the patterns seen in 4 cases
validator_change: Yes -- a generalized validator would need to check that explicit_non_identity_with pairs are symmetric and that no actor lists itself
artifact_migration_required: Retrofit only (all 4 existing artifacts already use these exact field names informally; formalizing them requires no renaming, only recognizing them as Draft V2-native rather than extensions)
public_display_change: None at Level 1/2 public display -- these remain Draft V2 section 10 Research-Only Fields
backward_compatibility: Full -- existing artifacts already populate compatible values; no data loss on adoption
risk: LOW -- the fields already exist informally and have been used consistently across three independent artifact-construction turns without confusion
alternative_rejected: REJECTED: a new first-class 'ActorContinuityClaim' entity (over-engineered for 4 optional descriptive fields); REJECTED: leaving continuity/mandate purely in free-text notes (current state -- fails to support machine-checkable discipline); REJECTED: a closed enum for mandate_status (would overfit to only the mandate patterns observed in 4 cases, none of which is exhaustive)
notes: Smallest change in this changeset: formalizes an already-converged informal practice rather than introducing new modeling concepts.

change_family: CF-01 Actor identity and mandate extension
current_v2_component: No structured way to record that two actors were deliberately compared and judged non-identical
proposed_v2_1_component: explicit_non_identity_with field (see CH-01) doubles as this mechanism -- listed here separately because the plan's own candidate list treats 'possible_predecessor_actor_ids'/'possible_successor_actor_ids' as a distinct concept from non-identity
problem_solved: Distinguishes 'never tested for identity' from 'tested and explicitly judged non-identical' -- Tiku V3's own 1662/1684 collectives currently rely entirely on free-text notes for this distinction
schema_change: No additional schema change beyond CH-01's explicit_non_identity_with field
validator_change: Minor -- same validator check as CH-01
alternative_rejected: REJECTED: separate possible_predecessor_actor_ids/possible_successor_actor_ids fields (per the plan's own CF-01 candidate list) -- these describe a DIFFERENT relationship (temporal succession, as tested in Sillida's own Bajang office-holder case, which PASSED without needing this field) and would conflate succession-testing with non-identity-testing if merged; kept as a future, separately-evaluated candidate if a genuine succession-chain failure is found
notes: This change is folded into CH-01's own field rather than proposed as a separate schema addition, to avoid field proliferation for what is fundamentally the same underlying need.

change_type: new relation type OR directional annotation (researcher decision required)
current_v2_component: COLLECTS_TOLL_FROM and CLAIMS_COMMODITY_MONOPOLY represent rights HELD, with no representation for rights RELEASED/EXEMPTED/WAIVED
proposed_v2_1_component: OPTION A (minimal): add a right_status field (values: HELD, GRANTED, EXEMPTED, RELINQUISHED, RENEWED) to existing toll/monopoly relation types, valid only alongside a required right_status_effective_date. OPTION B (structured): a CommercialRight/CommercialPrivilege object distinct from the PowerRelation model, with GRANTS/WAIVES/RELEASES/REVOKES/RENEWS/EXEMPTS as its own action vocabulary, per the plan's own CF-02
problem_solved: Removes the need to leave voluntary rights-relinquishment/exemption acts entirely unmodeled, closing the single most cross-case-corroborated gap in this synthesis
schema_change: Option A: minor (one new field + one new bounded enum on 2 existing relation types). Option B: major (a new object class outside the PowerRelation model)
controlled_vocabulary_change: Option A: new right_status enum (5 values). Option B: new action-type enum (6 values) plus a new right-type enum (6 values, per the plan's own CF-02 candidates)
validator_change: Both options require validator updates; Option B requires a substantially larger validator surface (a new entity class to check for uniqueness, orphan endpoints, etc., mirroring the existing actor/location/commodity/instrument pattern)
artifact_migration_required: Both options are additive only for existing artifacts (Tiku/Sillida's own toll relations remain valid; the relinquishment act itself would newly become representable, requiring a small artifact update, not a rebuild)
public_display_change: None at Level 1/2 -- 'a right was released' is a natural, non-technical public-display-safe fact, arguably MORE public-display-friendly than the current silent gap
backward_compatibility: Full for Option A (additive field); full for Option B (new object, no existing structure altered)
risk: Option A risk: LOW, but may prove too narrow if a right-modification act needs richer detail (multiple parties, partial release) than one status field can carry. Option B risk: MODERATE -- introduces the largest new schema surface area in this changeset from only 2 confirmed cases, risking over-engineering (as flagged in FCL-02's own risk_if_added)
alternative_rejected: REJECTED: a new relation type per right-action (e.g. RELINQUISHES_TOLL_TO, EXEMPTS_FROM_TOLL) -- directly violates the task's own explicit hard rule against case-specific relation proliferation, and would need a near-identical parallel type for every existing right-holding relation type; REJECTED: no-change (current state, leaves a 3x-cross-case-corroborated gap unaddressed)
researcher_decision: PENDING -- Option A vs Option B is the single most consequential open researcher decision in this changeset
notes: This synthesis recommends Option A (minimal field extension) as the SMALLEST defensible change per the plan's own change-design principle 'prefer the smallest model change that solves multiple failures,' while presenting Option B for researcher consideration given the plan's own explicit instruction to evaluate a structured object alternative.

current_v2_component: resistance_candidate annotation (Draft V2 section 3) has no target-actor field
proposed_v2_1_component: Add an OPTIONAL resistance_target_actor_id field (single actor_id, not a list, to avoid over-generalizing beyond the one confirmed use case) alongside the existing resistance_candidate field, used ONLY when the resistance target differs from the relation's own object
problem_solved: Prevents a resistance value from being silently misread as describing resistance toward the relation's own object when the source documents resistance toward a different actor
schema_change: Yes -- 1 new optional field on the existing resistance_candidate annotation only (annotation remains research-only throughout, per the task's own hard rule)
controlled_vocabulary_change: No enum change -- the new field holds an actor_id reference, not a new controlled vocabulary
validator_change: Minor -- a generalized validator would check the field references a valid actor_id when populated
artifact_migration_required: Retrofit only where needed (Tiku's own 1662 relations would populate it; all other cases' resistance_candidate uses are unaffected since their target already matches the relation's own object)
public_display_change: None -- resistance remains research-only at Level 1/2, this field does not change that
alternative_rejected: REJECTED: resistance_target_relation_type or resistance_scope (per the plan's own broader CF-05 candidate list) -- no case in V1-V4 demonstrates a need for anything beyond a single target-actor reference; proposing the narrower field first, with the broader ones deferred to REQUIRES_MORE_EVIDENCE pending a case that actually needs them
notes: Narrowest possible field to solve exactly the one documented case, per the plan's own minimal-change principle.

change_type: structured annotation extension on the existing observation entity (NOT a new relation type)
current_v2_component: EffectiveControlObservation entity exists (Draft V2, already used in Natal/Koto Tangah/Sillida) but has no structured fields for command-over-coerced-labor specifically
proposed_v2_1_component: Add OPTIONAL structured fields to the EffectiveControlObservation entity when its subject is a command relationship: coercion_status (enum: FREE, COERCED, CANNOT_DETERMINE), ability_to_refuse (enum: YES, NO, CANNOT_DETERMINE), political_intent (free text, explicitly NOT a controlled vocabulary, to avoid forcing a loyalty/resistance binary), voice_availability (enum: DOCUMENTED, ABSENT, CANNOT_DETERMINE)
supporting_cases: Sillida V4 (single case, non-independent evidence -- see FCL-06)
problem_solved: Gives the currently-freeform OBS_CONSTRAINED_AGENCY workaround a structured, machine-checkable, cross-case-comparable form, without creating a directed relation that could be misused to imply consent
schema_change: Yes -- 4 new optional fields on the EffectiveControlObservation entity (not a new entity class)
controlled_vocabulary_change: New bounded enums for coercion_status, ability_to_refuse, voice_availability (3 values each); political_intent deliberately left as free text, not an enum, to avoid forcing a premature classification of agency the sources do not support
validator_change: Moderate -- a generalized validator would need a NEW check family specifically verifying that no relation_type is EVER used where one of these fields is populated (i.e., constrained-agency observations must never simultaneously appear as a relation subject/object) -- this is the single most safety-critical validator requirement in this entire changeset
artifact_migration_required: Retrofit optional (Sillida's own existing observation can be reformatted to use the new structured fields, or left as-is; both remain valid)
public_display_change: None -- remains Draft V2 section 10 Research-Only; explicitly NEVER surfaces as a public relation category, per the task's own hard rule against implying voluntary alliance
risk: HIGH if implemented carelessly: any future misuse that allows a constrained-agency observation's subject/object pair to ALSO appear in a directed relation would silently reintroduce exactly the voluntary-alliance mischaracterization this change is meant to prevent -- the validator change (see above) is not optional, it is the change's own safety mechanism
alternative_rejected: REJECTED: DIRECTS_OPERATION_BY / DEPLOYS_GROUP_IN / COMMANDS_UNIT as new RELATION types (per the plan's own CF-06 candidate list) -- rejected specifically because ANY directed relation type between a commanding institution and a coerced group risks being read, or later reused, as implying a normal command-and-compliance relationship structurally similar to a voluntary one; an annotation-only extension on an existing OBSERVATION entity (never a relation) is the safer structural choice, at the cost of the relationship remaining less prominently modeled than a first-class relation would be
researcher_decision: PENDING -- this is the highest-priority single decision in this synthesis given the severity finding in FCL-06
notes: This is the most carefully-scoped proposal in the changeset: it deliberately trades relational prominence for safety against consent-implying misuse, directly honoring the task's own explicit and repeated hard rule.

current_v2_component: No representation for third-party arbitration/fine outcomes distinct from toll, lease, or monopoly relations
proposed_v2_1_component: A DisputeSettlement object (Draft V2 KEEP_RESEARCH_ONLY-class, alongside NamedCollective/DocumentaryReport/StrategicInteraction) with fields: disputing_actor_ids, mediating_actor_ids, paying_actor_ids, receiving_actor_ids, resource_or_object, amount_or_share_as_written, settlement_date, source_document_ids -- per the plan's own CF-07 candidate design
problem_solved: Allows tracking and future cross-case comparison of a plausibly-systematic colonial pattern (VOC capturing disproportionate shares of dispute settlements) that is currently invisible because it has no representable form at all
schema_change: Yes -- a new entity class (largest schema surface area proposed for a single-case failure in this changeset)
controlled_vocabulary_change: No relation-type or annotation-enum change -- this is a structured object, not a controlled vocabulary addition
validator_change: Significant -- a new entity class requires the same validator scaffolding as commodities/instruments/locations (uniqueness, orphan-reference checks)
artifact_migration_required: None required for existing artifacts (Sillida's own 1679 fine detail remains valid as free-text notes; adopting the new object is optional, additive)
public_display_change: None at Level 1/2 initially -- could inform a future 'dispute settlements and fines' public category if researcher-approved later, but no such category exists yet
risk: MODERATE -- proposing a full new entity class from a SINGLE case is the largest schema-to-evidence ratio in this changeset; risk of building infrastructure for a pattern that may not recur
alternative_rejected: REJECTED: forcing the 1679 fine into COLLECTS_TOLL_FROM (a one-time punitive payment is not an ongoing toll, misrepresenting its own nature); REJECTED: a new USES_ADJUDICATED_FORCE_AGAINST-style relation type (a fine allocation involves 3+ parties with different roles -- paying, receiving, mediating -- which the dyadic PowerRelation model cannot cleanly represent, exactly the reason a structured object rather than a relation type is proposed)
notes: Recommend explicit researcher deferral pending a second case (REQUIRES_MORE_EVIDENCE-adjacent) UNLESS the researcher judges the systemic-extraction-pattern risk (see FCL-07 risk_if_ignored) significant enough to build ahead of a second confirming case.
